changes: Builds now matter. Your abilities deal more damage the more your Physical-vs-Arcane training leans toward their school, up to x2.25 for going all-in; an even split gets no bonus. Physical builds start fast but slow down in later zones, Arcane builds start slow and finish strong, and Hybrid builds get there too, just much more slowly.
Monsters in later zones resist weapons (Sunken Crypt 20%, Ember Caverns 35%, Frostbound Peaks 50%) and deeper zones resist a little spell damage too. Resistances are shown on the Zones page.

Spells start weaker but gain extra power from every point of Arcana (Arcane mastery). Arcana now costs the same to train as Might, and Willpower also grants +0.75 max HP per point so casters can survive without Grit.
The game is slower and longer: monsters get tougher faster with depth, so reaching Frostbound Peaks now takes a focused build around 200 to 240 hours of play instead of about 60.

Three new attributes, one per group: Endurance (Physical: max Stamina and Stamina regeneration), Spirit (Arcane: Mana regeneration and less damage taken) and Precision (Utility: Crit Chance and Crit Damage). Weapon abilities no longer run dry on Stamina once you have some Endurance. Existing saves start them at 0.

Monsters are tougher to match: HP and damage now grow a little faster per depth (Whispering Woods 4% to 4.15%, other zones 3.5% to 3.8%). Early floors barely change; deep floors and zone-gate bosses are noticeably harder.
Fortune's extra gear drop chance is now diminishing (up to +50%) instead of passing a guaranteed drop. Its Focus bonus is unchanged. Fixed the Fortune, Willpower and Speed descriptions.

New: Build presets on the Automation page (Physical, Arcane, Hybrid) set every autobuyer weight at once, so Focus stops going into stats and abilities your build doesn't use. The weight lists are grouped like Training and Abilities.

Inventory: Equip all upgrades fills empty slots and takes every overall upgrade in one click. Items are now labelled Upgrade, About the same or Worse by the overall change, with a hint when a worse item still improves something. Rows show tags for augments, MAX level and reforge-ready, lists use whole levels, and on wide screens Equipped and Inventory sit side by side.

Gear rework: 11 equipment slots (Head, Body, Legs, Feet, Hands, Main Hand, Off Hand, Neck, Back and two Rings). You now wear either a weapon or a wand, and either armor or a robe, so builds lean physical or arcane. Trinkets became real pieces (e.g. the Adept Orb is an off hand, the Adept Tome became the Adept Hood). Existing saves move over automatically; where two worn items now share a slot, the one matching your main ability type stays on and the other goes to your inventory.
Every set now has a piece for every slot, with a new 10-piece bonus. New pieces: helms, greaves, leggings, cloaks, sabatons and more across all five sets.
New: compare and equip whole sets. Each set on the Inventory page shows what wearing it would change overall, and Equip set puts on your best owned copy of every piece in one click.

Inventory redesign: equipped gear and your inventory are compact lists, and selecting an item shows everything about it in one panel: stats, what equipping it would change, augments, fusing, reforging and salvage. On phones the panel opens from the bottom.

Upgrade / Sidegrade / Worse now judge your whole character, not just the item's own numbers. Set bonuses gained or broken and augments count, and each stat is valued by what it actually does for you. Items show the overall % change, and the panel breaks it down into Offense, Defense, Sustain, Resources and Economy.
Each equipped slot shows how many items in your inventory would improve it, and selecting a slot lists every candidate with an Equip button.
Trinkets now fit either trinket slot. Pick the slot yourself, or let Equip choose the better one.
Augments can be removed for free, and equipping a replacement moves the old item's augments over automatically.
Salvage buttons now show what you'll get, and single salvage asks for confirmation. Salvage all worse keeps set pieces unless you tick include set pieces.
Inventory can be searched, sorted (best first, rarity, level, name) and filtered to hide worse items.
Crafting cards say whether the piece would be an upgrade over what you wear, and Imbue has moved to its own tab on the Crafting page.
Crafting: show or hide each set (and gear without a set), or show only the sets you are wearing. The choice is remembered in this browser.
Reforge requirements no longer reveal the name of a zone you have not unlocked yet.
Fixed the top bar on phones: HP, Stamina and Mana now share a row instead of running off the screen.

Gear comparisons now know when Stamina or Mana runs out: more Speed only counts as far as your resources can pay for the extra casts, and Stamina, Mana, Endurance and Spirit count toward Offense when you are running dry.

Set gear now carries the new attributes: Woodland Vanguard and Crypt Warden pieces have Endurance instead of Stamina Cap, Woodland Adept and Frost Sentinel pieces have Spirit instead of Regeneration, and Ember Zealot has Precision instead of Crit Chance. Several set bonuses now grant Endurance, Spirit or Precision. The Gear Stats Overview lists the new attributes.

Fixed offline progress being much weaker than online at high Speed: catch-up runs in one-second steps and each ability could only fire once per step. Fast abilities now fire as often offline as they would while you watch.

New: Pause in Settings. Time stops (no combat, regeneration or Focus) while you can still train, equip and craft. A Paused chip in the top bar resumes the game, paused time does not count as offline time, and reloading resumes.
Abilities, Training and the combat ability bar are grouped: Physical (Stamina) and Arcane (Mana) abilities, and Physical, Arcane and Utility stats.
Fixed the Combat page on phones: the combat log now sits below the fight instead of squeezing it.

Fixed a faint loop: a monster could keep its attack fully charged through fainting and hit you the instant you recovered, over and over. Its attack timer now resets when you faint and when you recover.

Fixed training cost rising with the stat's value instead of with how many times you trained it, which cancelled out every stat-gain bonus from Recall, Ascend and perks. Training now shows the stat value and its level (times trained) separately, and the buy buttons match what you actually get.
Lower-rarity copies of an item you've reforged now feed the higher-rarity version as partial levels, instead of piling up as separate, useless items.

Duplicate gear no longer fuses automatically from the start. Duplicates wait on the item as pending levels until you press Fuse (or Fuse all), or you can have them auto-salvaged. Auto-fusing unlocks after 5 Recalls, and saves that already have 5 keep it on.

Duplicates of an item already at its level cap are now salvaged for Focus and materials instead of disappearing. Maxed items show a MAX badge and how many duplicates were salvaged, and Crafting won't make copies past the cap.

New Automation page: choose how duplicates are handled, and after enough Recalls unlock Auto-train (2 Recalls) and Auto-upgrade abilities (3 Recalls). Each stat and ability gets a weight, and a spending limit keeps Focus free for crafting.

Inventory rework: equipped gear is shown as a grid of slots. Inventory items are sorted best-first with an Upgrade / Sidegrade / Worse badge and can be filtered by slot. New buttons: Fuse all, and Salvage all worse.
Crafting now shows one card per item with a rarity picker, how the owned copy is doing, and the same ×1/×5/×10/×25/Max buttons as Training.
Equipped items now show their socketed augments, and you can socket augments without unequipping.
The top bar now shows your current zone and depth (click it to jump to Combat), replacing the Speed readout.

Features you can't use yet now stay hidden. The Inventory, Crafting and Automation tabs appear with your first item, and Zones with your second zone. Locked automation features and the next zone show as ????? with only their unlock requirement. Statistics only lists zones, abilities, materials and counters you've actually reached.

New: Milestones. Lifetime totals such as monsters defeated, Focus earned or bosses beaten grant small permanent bonuses. Track your progress on the Statistics page; the next milestone stays hidden until you reach it.
New: Imbue augments on the Crafting page. Spend surplus materials to permanently strengthen a learned augment everywhere it's socketed. Augment descriptions now show their real current strength.
New: a "While you were away" summary when you return after more than a minute: time away, kills, Focus, depth pushed, loot, levels gained and milestones reached.
New: a Recall timing panel on the Prestige page showing Focus per minute, Echoes per hour if you Recall now, and this run's best rate, with a hint once the rate is past its peak.
The Crypt Warden, Ember Zealot and Frost Sentinel sets can now be reforged up to legendary, each tier gated by depth in its own zone. The legendary tiers also drop from those zones' bosses.
Reforge depth requirements now use your deepest depth ever, so a reforge you've earned no longer locks again after a Recall.

Added a full Reforge upgrade path for Whispering Woods gear: every Vanguard/Adept piece can now be reforged common -> uncommon -> rare -> epic -> legendary from the Inventory page, each tier gated behind reaching a deeper part of the zone and costing materials plus Focus.
Legendary gear can also now drop directly from bosses deep in a zone.
Gear leveling from duplicates now caps per rarity, so grinding one common item can no longer out-power reforging into a higher tier.
Prestige is reorganized into separate Recall and Ascend tabs, and stays hidden from the main navigation until you're actually close to unlocking it.
The Guide page now only shows articles relevant to your progress (e.g. Gear and Crafting stay hidden until you've found your first item).
Training and Abilities now use direct ×1/×5/×10/×25/Max buy buttons instead of a separate quantity toggle.

Reworked several pages (Guide, Settings, Prestige, Training, Abilities, Inventory) to use the full width of the screen instead of a narrow centered column, and fixed Inventory action buttons overlapping on smaller cards.
Added new prestige perks, including Keen Edge, Heavy Hitter, and Vampiric Touch.
Fixed fast, cheap abilities starving slower ones of Stamina and Mana, and doubled base Stamina/Mana caps.
Fixed several abilities not counting toward their own usage statistics.
The combat log now collapses repeated hits into a single running line instead of flooding out other events.
Recall's permanent stat-gain bonus now scales with the deepest depth you've ever Recalled at, closing an exploit where recalling shallowly on repeat out-paced genuine progress.
Ascend's permanent stat-gain bonus now scales with your biggest single Ascend payout for the same reason.

Added a compounding Boss Power bonus so your damage keeps pace with monster scaling at extreme depth, and zones now unlock after clearing a set number of that zone's bosses rather than requiring a full depth clear.
Fixed a rare crash and performance issue when Overkill chained through many kills at once.
Added the Speed stat, player HP, and monster counter-attacks on their own real-time timer.
Replaced the ability priority list with independent per-ability cooldowns; Active mode manual clicks now deal bonus damage.
Replaced random gear rolls with a curated item catalog, gear sets with set bonuses, and duplicate items now auto-fuse into levels instead of cluttering your inventory.
Added gear comparison, augment descriptions, a gear stats overview, and item salvage to the Inventory page.
Reworked the UI into full-page tabs with a new HUD header and dark fantasy theme.
Initial release: Stamina/Mana/Focus resources, Whispering Woods zone, basic combat, gear, augments, and Recall/Ascend prestige.
